title: The Himalayan War
summary: The ancient conflict between Akashics and the forerunners of the Euthanatos.

claims.text: Many events of the war are shielded against Time sight, some by old strategic wards and some by the reborn participants who would rather keep their past lives private.
Both Traditions discourage open study of the war, though modern death mages are more willing to dig and sometimes ask Akashics for help.
A modern chronology puts Akashic entry into India around 950 BCE, with doctrinal quarrels keeping them in northern camps.

title: The Chodona
summary: The Eight-Spoked Wheel of the Law that united the death mages.

claims.text: At the founding gathering the delegates first quarrelled over burial customs and accused one another of meddling with the Wheel.
The Sirdar pointed out that each was repeating the same fears their home cultures held about them, and talk turned to shared purpose.
Ten years later they set that purpose down as the Eight-Spoked Wheel of the Law, the Chodona; by 1314 the Wheel reached from Nepal to Ireland.

title: Chakravanti
summary: The oldest Thanatoic sect, which defines the Tradition.

claims.text: The Chakravanti trace their line to the Himalayan War and the driving of the Akashic Brotherhood out of southern India.
The sect is split between traditionalists such as the Natatapas, who see new beliefs as confirming the Cycle, and Lhaksmists, who think new ideas question the old orthodoxy.
Its core belief is that souls are eternal and reborn, lives rise or fall by karma, and siddhi let a skilled mage trade karmic traits with the oversoul.

title: Lhaksmists and Devasu
summary: Two sects of the Chakravanti: fortune's devotees and Rudra's warriors.

claims.text: Lhaksmists began as a Natatapa subcult devoted to the Goddess of Fortune and now read chaos maths, information theory and gambling as signs of the Goddess.
A Lhaksmist may let a coin or dice decide a weighty choice, treating luck as a test of will against karma, and usually keeps the result open to reading.
The Devasu channel Rudra, archer of the Vedic gods, through yoga and martial arts to defend Thanatoic lands, while internal threats are left to the Albireo.

title: Madzimbabwe
summary: Southern African death mages tied to Great Zimbabwe.

claims.text: Legend says the Madzimbabwe came to the Convocation seeking the Sirdar Rustam, who had visited Africa on a last voyage and never come back.
Thanatoic history paints them as a young faction, but they had existed as an organised group for centuries.
They link themselves to Great Zimbabwe, a meeting place for southern Africa's Awakened, and still prize the smaller stone courts in the region, many of which hold strong Nodes.

title: Hierochthonoi
summary: Greek priests of the earth among the Euthanatos.

claims.text: Rather than offer sacrifices, the Hierochthonoi give themselves to duty, following chthonic cults as old as Homer's day.
After Troy fell, sages spoke of the Ixos, sorcerer-spies said to have slipped Myrmidons into Ilion and to lie behind Agamemnon's death and the trials of Odysseus.
Chthonic gods like the Fates were honoured in caves and wild shrines, and Alexander's generals hired early Hierochthonoi as healers and necromancers.

title: Golden Chalice
summary: The elite assassins of the Euthanatos.

claims.text: Apart from the Golden Chalice, no one joins a Vrata without first proving themselves in another sect.
Tryouts are held yearly at a European estate that changes each time, mixing brutal physical tests, ambushes, alchemical riddles and staged betrayals around the clock.
Candidates need ratings of 4 in any five of Firearms, Melee, Stealth, Dodge, Technology, Subterfuge, Occult or Enigmas, two Spheres at 3, and one other rare gift; even that does not ensure entry.

title: Spinning the soul
summary: Why duty is the source of Thanatoic magic.

claims.text: To the Euthanatos the Chodona is not a moral rule laid on top of magic; duty is what makes their magic possible, since only a pure soul can touch the Akasha beneath reality.
Save for Gilgul, the Atman, or Avatar, is held to be divine and indestructible, learning its own nature over many lives and able to reach Moksa.
The Wheel gives the Tellurian its shape by enforcing cause and effect; if every being could bend reality, the world would fall back into chaos.
